summary: Customer sees credits applied twice on March invoice after regional postback failover
description:
Issue summary:
Customer LumenLogic reports that their March invoice (invoice_id: INV-2026-03-07-LL) has two near-identical credit line items totaling $12,400, which produce a negative balance. The credits are labeled as 'hourly-smoothing-credit' and 'promotional-rate-override-credit' but each appears twice with the same amounts and reference metadata.

Impact:
- Customer billing shows negative line item; finance cannot finalize month-end.
- Customer is on Dedicated and expects predictable reserved-rate billing.
- Customer requests immediate explanation and provisional reversal to finalize their internal accounting.

Environment:
- Dedicated pool: redwood-dedicated-us-east-2 (LumenLogic org id: org_0xLL)
- Billing pipeline: postback-ingest -> postback-processor -> charge-apply job -> invoice-generator
- Peak activity window: 2026-03-07 01:47:00 - 01:59:00 UTC (microburst batch embed job resumed)

Steps to reproduce (as reported by customer):
1) Resume previously paused batch embedding job at 2026-03-07T01:47:12Z.
2) Job emits burst of 130k tokens and multiple postbacks.
3) At 01:48:20 UTC their reserved pool experienced a brief failover to eu-west for some routing requests.
4) Invoice generated on 2026-03-07 contains duplicate credit lines.

Customer-provided evidence:
- Invoice excerpt (sanitized): two entries each 'hourly-smoothing-credit' $6,200 and two 'promo-rate-override' $0.00 (promo displayed but duplicate credit applied).
- Postback ids (sample): pb_9a1f7c_01, pb_9a1f7c_02, pb_9a1f7c_02-replay
- Slack thread: #support-lumenlogic (link provided in private)

Requested outcome:
1) Explanation for why credits were duplicated.
2) Immediate provisional correction or invoice adjustment to allow customer to close month-end.
3) Permanent fix to prevent repeat occurrences and a timeline for reconciliation.
comments: 2026-03-10 - Maya Patel: Created ticket after customer uploaded invoice PDF and sample postback logs. Asking for provisional credit reversal. Assigned to Billing team.
2026-03-10 - Ethan Ross (Support): Acknowledged receipt, requested raw postback payloads and message digests. Escalated to SRE and Billing for triage. SLA first response target set to 2026-03-13.

2026-03-11 - Priya Sharma (SRE): Initial triage shows repeated postbacks with different region tags within 18s window. We see event_id duplicate but dedup-key in processor is org_id + request_timestamp (not event_id). Attaching query results to internal INT ticket.

2026-03-11 - Carlos Medina (Billing): Correlated credits in charge-apply logs for org_0xLL: two successful charge reversal runs for the same logical event. Candidate cause: replayed postback (pb_9a1f7c_02-replay) bypassed dedupe and triggered credit path twice.

2026-03-12 - Ethan Ross (Support): Informed customer we have a provisional plan: apply an interim invoice adjustment to neutralize duplicate credits while we complete a full reconciliation. Requested explicit approval to issue a provisional debit to balance invoice.
2026-03-12 - LumenLogic Billing Contact: Approved provisional adjustment; asked for permanent fix ETA and assurance this won't reoccur during their next batch window.
investigation_notes: Query of postback-ingest table (producer_ts between 2026-03-07T01:46:50Z and 2026-03-07T01:49:00Z) returned three distinct records with identical event_id but different region_tag fields (us-east, eu-west, us-east-replay).

postback-processor logs show dedupe check used key: concat(org_id, '|', floor(request_timestamp/60)) which groups by minute bucket and misses exact event_id collisions when replays shift timestamps by <60s.
charge-apply job is idempotent when presented with same postback_id; however, replayed messages used a suffixed postback_id (pb_..._replay) and bypassed idempotency, re-triggering credit path.

Billing code path: promotional-rate-override logic applied after smoothing-credit calculation; the second run re-evaluated smoothing and issued another credit because the first credit had been marked 'applied' but not yet reconciled to invoice when replay arrived.

Reproduction locally: simulated a replay with modified region_tag and postback_id variation results in duplicate credit generation. Patch hypothesis: strengthen dedupe key to include event_id and idempotency token (postback_id canonicalization).
resolution_notes: 2026-03-12 - Provisional action: Billing created manual adjustment invoice line (ADJ-642579) reversing the duplicate credits totaling $12,400 so the customer's invoice is balanced. Customer notified and provided adjusted PDF.

2026-03-12 - Hotfix deployed (billing-recon v1.2.3): postback-processor dedupe now uses canonical_event_id + org_id + region_shard to avoid minute-bucket collisions and normalizes postback_id suffixes to respect idempotency. Patch merged: github.com/redwood-inference/postback-processor/pull/745

Permanent reconciliation plan (next steps): Run full retro reconciliation for 2026-03-07 across affected dedicated pools and generate converse adjustments for any other orgs impacted. Billing to run job by 2026-03-15 and publish report to linked Confluence page.
Monitoring: Added a transient alert that triggers when more than one credit of the same type and amount is applied to the same org within a 2-minute window. Alert routed to #billing and on-call SRE.
Customer follow-up: LumenLogic confirmed adjusted invoice and accepted provisional reversal. They requested confirmation after retro reconciliation that there will be no net unexpected debit.
